clause_evidence.finding: Where an Integration assists in or generates content for employment-related decisions or communications, the user is responsible for reviewing and approving that content before submission. AI-generated postings, messages and other communications are subject to Upwork's ToS and the user is responsible for compliance including applicable AI disclosure obligations.

Upwork's Terms of Use fraud clause prohibits 'using generative AI or other tools to substantially bolster your job proposals or work product if such use is restricted by your client or violates any third-party's rights.' The Optional Contract Terms separately allow the buyer to contractually disallow GenAI tools on the engagement.
clause_evidence.scope: Upwork freelancers, proposals and work product

clause_evidence.finding: Upwork MCP server: AI tools can perform hiring/job actions directly, but actions that change anything are previewed and require the account holder's explicit confirmation - assisted workflow, not unattended execution. The account holder remains responsible for the agent's configuration and instructions.
Fiverr permits AI-assisted content and services, but the freelancer remains accountable for customized, original work; AI is not treated as a substitute for the freelancer's own skill and judgement.

Study-level instrument explicitly states: 'No AI assistance or VPN use is allowed during screening or participation.' Demonstrates the specificity-wins rule - a listing-level ban overrides platform default.

Recommended informed-consent language: 'Participants must be living individuals'; 'Participants must take the survey in good faith'; 'AI-generated/Bot responses will automatically be discarded'; incentives are not paid where fraud is determined.

UserTesting added LinkedIn respondent verification and employs AI-based detection, behavioural checks and human review so insights come from 'real people - not bots, not fraudsters, and not falsified personas.'
Prolific's authenticity check detects AI content with 98.7% accuracy; clear study instructions cut AI use by 61%. Detection is an operational control, not just a policy statement.

American Association for Public Opinion Research task force deemed synthetic responses 'the most risky' of AI applications to public polling; recommends validate-then-simulate (establish agreement with human data first, scale generation only after).

Distinguishes full delegation (AI originates response content - corrupts qualitative patterns directly) from partial mediation (AI assists writing - still biases aggregate estimates by compressing response variance and moderating extreme positions). Both matter; neither is neutral.

steps.rule: Read the governing instrument at three levels; most-specific wins. 1) Platform ToS 2) study/listing-specific instructions 3) contract or screener terms. A study-level 'no AI assistance' overrides platform silence. A client contract disallowance overrides platform default (Upwork Optional Contract Terms pattern). If no instrument mentions AI, default to G2-G4 rather than assuming permission.

Apply Upwork's own test: does the AI step SUBSTANTIALLY BOLSTER the proposal/work product - i.e. does it originate substance the human did not author? Originating = prohibited without explicit permission. Expressing what the human already authored = permitted-in-principle, subject to G3.

The human must be the source of judgment, opinion, experience, skill and data. AI may reformulate the human's own authored content (clarity, grammar, structure). AI may never originate content that stands as the human's beliefs, experience, qualifications or research data. Full delegation fails always; partial mediation still degrades the estimand (OSF contamination finding).

Before submission, the human must review, understand and be able to defend the output without the tool. If you cannot explain it, do not submit it. AI-driven platform actions (Upwork MCP pattern) require explicit preview-and-confirm - never unattended execution.

verdicts.DISCLOSE: passes G1-G4 but the human-side disclosure obligation in G1 is triggered (e.g. client contract requires AI-use disclosure, study debrief asks about tools). Disclose tool name and extent.
verdicts.PERMIT: passes all four gates AND no disclosure obligation triggered.
verdicts.PROHIBIT: fails any gate. Typical fails: AI-originated screener answers (G1+G3 - fabricated credential), fully synthetic survey responses (G1+G2+G3 - fraud), mass auto-submitted proposals (G1+G4 - unattended execution), undisclosed AI-written deliverable where client contract restricts it (G1+G2).

worked_examples.step: Fixing grammar in a study's open-ended answer you wrote yourself, on a study with no AI instruction.
worked_examples.step_gates: G1: no prohibition at any level. G2: does not originate substance. G3: human authored the content. G4: reviewable.

worked_examples.step: Having an AI write screener answers to qualify for a study you do not genuinely qualify for.
worked_examples.step_gates: G1: falsified-persona policy (UserTesting) + good-faith requirement (BSU IRB). G3: AI originates the qualifying data. = fabricated credential.

worked_examples.conclusion: PROHIBIT unless client consents in contract terms
worked_examples.step: Delivering an Upwork client's report where the analysis is AI-originated and the client contract is silent on AI.
worked_examples.step_gates: G2: substantially bolsters the work product. Default is prohibition without explicit client permission; Optional Contract Terms exist for exactly this.

worked_examples.step: Using Upwork's MCP/Claude connector to draft proposals you personally review and submit.
worked_examples.step_gates: G1: integrations terms require review before submission. G4: explicit confirmation is the mechanism. Unattended submission = prohibit.

worked_examples.step: Using AI to summarize your own interview notes for a freelance report, disclosing the summarizer if asked.
worked_examples.step_gates: G2: expresses your own material. G3: human is the data source. G4: you can defend the summary.

payload.note_to_rivet: The hard part is G1: platforms differ wildly and study-level instructions override defaults. The most reliable single habit is reading the listing/contract before touching any tool. The riskiest blind spot is G3-partial-mediation: people assume light AI help is neutral, but the OSF finding shows it still biases aggregate estimates - in research work, 'just cleaning up the wording' is not harmless at scale.
